originStory:
The year is 6999. The races are gathering at the summit of Preacher`s Peak for the nearing New Millennium celebration. Every millennium this celebration is host to the largest gathering of all the races in one place. Warborn, Mechanizer, Sunwalker, Moonwalker, Prim, and Subterrian all join together to celebrate their ancestors` discovery of Spirit Aura as well as the feats they have accomplished with it.
Since the discovery of Spirit Aura, all of the races have expanded past the reaches of their home atmosphere on Thrae and travelled far into the galaxy, but never past the galactic border. It seems that the closer they get to the edge of the galaxy, the greater trouble they have controlling their Spirit Aura. Cases of seemingly random explosions, fires, systems malfunctioning, and worst of all, spontaneous death have been reported by the ships who have wandered closest to the edge of our galaxy. As for the reason why, it has yet to be discovered and has proven to be a rather persistent barrier to space travel.
Even though it is believed all the races come from a common ancestral species, each race is quite different from one another because of the way they interact with and utilize Spirit Aura.
The Prim are a faith-driven people. They remain on Thrae because they are beings that worship the land of Thrae itself and wish not to abandon their home. Part of their belief is that their Spirit Aura`s strength is directly correlated to Thrae. They have relatively stronger Spirit Aura on average because of their strong belief system. The Prim are responsible for taking care of the preparations for the millennial celebration because of their choice to reside exclusively on Thrae.
The Orcs are warriors at heart. They are bested by none in brute strength, so they provide invaluable laborers to The Great Journey. The power of an Orc`s Spirit Aura is usually linked to his physical strength, his abnormally robust vitality, and his resistance to natural afflictions, such as weather and poison.
Subterrians are great miners. They use Spirit Aura to power their excavation machines and have contributed to The Great Journey through their ability to mine and gather valuable resources from the planets they come across. They are best at pinpointing where the most valuable minerals are, which is useful when gathering resources for smithing tools and weapons.
The Progenitor bloodline is strongly connected to the universe`s flow of Spirit Aura, so they are able to bend Spirit Aura much more effectively than the average user.
Each race has a “Champion” who is the person with the strongest control over Spirit Aura out of all other members of their race. Champions are hailed as celebrities and every year there
The universe is split into domains, each with its own flow of Spirit Aura. We refer to these domains as “galaxies”. The Progenitors are the first beings in history to gain control over the flow of Spirit Aura. The rest of the domains (other galaxies) are home to different kinds of Spirit Aura. When the Progenitors get near the other kinds of Aura that exist, they begin to feel the suffering and pain that The First had to endure when he made his trip to Preacher`s Peak. If their soul is strong enough and their willpower sufficient, they can adapt to the new flow of Spirit Aura just as The First did. However, this challenge is not for the faint of heart. Just because you are a descendent of The First and carry his powers within you does not mean your soul is automatically powerful enough to adjust. This comes down to the individual.
Being a good person, you see, is not as subjective as people may think. At the core of all things that exist, there is a concept that is universally sought after: perpetuity. Without things to fill the universe, it is nothing but an empty void. There is no light or dark, loud or quiet, happy or sad. Just nothing. Because of this fact, one is able to realize that there is a very simple formula for being a good person: to behave in such a way towards yourself and towards others, unconditionally, such that you enable and assist the perpetual existence of all beings, until they meet an appropriate end.
A person that has given themselves the chance to peer into that void, to realize the true terror that nothingness represents, is a person the universe will recognize as an ally of all things. This is what it takes to adapt the essence of one`s soul to an unfamiliar flow of Spirit Aura, and it`s is how The First discovered the presence of Spirit Aura. It is through this mindset that the main character will lead the way into new galaxies.

gdd.marketing:
MARKETING
Target Audience
My target audience is fans of science-fiction and fantasy alike. Ages 15-25. Players who are driven by a deep story will enjoy the most. Fans of action-rpg games as well as dialogue-heavy games will also have a good time with this game. Intended rating will be M - Mature for violence and adult language.
Platform
The game will be primarily developed for PC only, but there is certainly potential for mobile iOS and Android releases in the future. PC exclusively at first because it is only me and it will be easier for testing to just be able to playtest on the same machine as the development environment.
Competitors?
There are plenty of RPG fantasy games out there, as well as RPG science-fiction games. However, I’m developing a combination of the two, which I’ve personally never seen done before. This being the case, I think my competition for this specific genre of game isn’t as heavy as it would be for something more commonly made, like traditional RPG’s and FPS’s.
gdd.gameplay:
The overworld is a free-roam area that the player can wander around in, restrictively. There will be mandatory enemies that guard other sections of the overworld. These enemies will act as “mini-bosses” and will be tougher than the average enemy of the area they guard.
There are towns and other ‘safe zones’ that the player can enter that do not have any enemies. This is where shops, most NPCs, and rest stops will be located. Resting in a safe zone will make that safe zone the player’s spawn point should they die or reload their save file.
Combat will take place in a separate *scene* than the overworld.
In the overworld, there will be unique enemy sprites wandering around outside of towns that will give you an idea of what you will be fighting against.
The fight starts when you interact with the enemy or when the enemy interacts with you. However, there may be extra enemies in the group that aren’t revealed until you start the fight.
The combat will follow Action-RPG guidelines in that the player may move about freely during a fight and the enemies will actively give chase and try to hit the player with basic attacks and/or damaging abilities. Once the player’s health drops to 0, it is game over and they will be placed back in the last safe zone they rested in.

Combat’s default control scheme will be as follows (Mouse + Keyboard):
1 - uses assigned ability
2 - uses assigned ability
3 - uses assigned ability
4 - uses ultimate ability
Right Click (Hold) - Block
Left Click - Basic Attack
Q/E - Switch Equipped Gear
WASD - Move
Character Stats:
Strength - effects combat damage from basic melee attacks
Dexterity - effects weapon swapping speed and melee attack speed
Vitality - effects how much total HP player has
Focus - effects how many focus points(mana) you have and how much damage abilities do
Agility - effects movement speed and chance to dodge
Resolve - effects how quickly stamina regenerates
Perception - effects ability cooldown and chance to hit
Corruption - for every 5 points in this skill, creatures will give 5% less total experience. This skill can be lowered with in-game currency and is increased by certain enemies the player can (sometimes must) kill. The enemies that give Corruption experience will also give better experience in other stats than average creatures. Corruption’s de-buff will not affect its own experience progression.
Player earns XP for creature kills. Each stat has its own progress bar. Different creatures give progress to different stats. Enemies that are good counters to certain stats are the ones that give the most experience for that stat (Enemies that drain health will give the most points in Vitality, enemies difficult to dodge will give most points in Agility, etc.). The player goes up in total level after 2 points are gained in any individual stat. Total level slightly effects every stat and makes the player’s abilities do more damage. When the player’s total level reaches a multiple of 5, the progress experience bar for each stat resets to 0.
NPC interactions will have text boxes that pop up on the bottom of the screen to display dialogue. Some NPCs will have unique dialogue choices for the player to make, but many of them will have generic things the player can say to them. However, certain NPCs will give unique/informative responses to things you say to them, even if the dialogue option is generic. This will force players to interact with every (or most) NPC they come across. On the grand scale of the game’s story, very few NPCs will have an effect based on dialogue choice. The main purpose of NPC interaction will be to give the player hints about gameplay and/or unlock unique items that otherwise would not be available. For example, a generic NPC in the tutorial town will have basic dialogue choices the player can make. If the player chooses the correct things to say to this NPC they will receive an item that makes the tutorial area a little easier.
gdd.art:
2D pixel sprites (64x64, 128x128, etc.) will make up most of the in-game assets
Cutscenes will be few and far between, but they will be rendered separately and contain a bit more detail than the in-game sprites. Similar overall art-style, but with more detail than the basic sprites.
I want every basic action to have an equally basic animation. This is because the abilities that both the player and the enemies can perform will have slightly more detailed and grand animations. I don’t want the walking animation to be so detailed that it takes away from the splendor of actually performing an attack or other related combat action.
